purpose: Cross-vertical ElevenLabs Simulation Tests for Atlas Web Studio local-business web-design outreach.

dynamic_variables.website_domain_cost_note: domain costs are separate and should be confirmed before anything paid
dynamic_variables.website_price_disclosure_rule: only discuss paid website pricing when the buyer directly asks about price, cost, money, hidden fees, or what happens after the free mockup

evaluation_repair_notes.accepted_send_without_contact: If the buyer accepts the send path before giving contact details, the agent should ask for the email or other approved send path before ending.
evaluation_repair_notes.unanswered_terminal_question: A final buyer turn that asks a new clear question, such as when the email will arrive or whether it will be sent there, is not a completed close unless the agent receives and answers another turn.
evaluation_repair_notes.delivery_timing_repair: If the buyer says timing was not answered, the agent should answer timing directly and avoid repeating the same full send/reply sentence.
evaluation_repair_notes.busy_two_option_compression: If the buyer offers both callback and email paths, the expected concise shape is `I can do both. Which would you prefer?`
evaluation_repair_notes.analogy_and_perspective: A plain analogy or perspective check is acceptable when it stays non-guaranteed and helps the buyer judge website trust or clarity.
evaluation_repair_notes.short_non_guarantee: The agent should prefer short wording such as `I can't promise that.` or `Not as a guarantee.` and must not use long wording such as `I can't promise that a website will automatically...` unless a stricter compliance boundary is needed.
evaluation_repair_notes.name_capture: For owner or manager conversations where no name is known and the call is not busy, gatekeeper, refusal, or terminal, the agent should answer the direct concern first, then ask who it is speaking with in the same non-terminal turn; if missed, it must ask before the next value explanation. Do not fail if the buyer gave their name earlier in the call.
evaluation_repair_notes.stronger_value_mechanism: After a short no or non-guarantee boundary, the agent should use a stronger campaign-safe mechanism such as a search-friendly page people can check before calling, service-area/service-match clarity, trust before a call, one shareable link, proof-before-purchase, or a local SEO foundation that helps Google understand services and area without promising rankings. Weak filler such as clearer page, something to judge, potential customers something to judge, or initial judgments should fail when used as the main value answer.
evaluation_repair_notes.public_profile_lookup_handoff: If the campaign permits it and the buyer explicitly says the contact email is on a public business source such as Facebook, Google, or the business website, the agent may accept that as a post-call lookup handoff. It must not claim it has already found or sent to that email.
evaluation_repair_notes.natural_two_step_email_close: buyer provides email; agent confirms normalized email; buyer confirms; agent closes. do not fail if the simulated conversation ends immediately after the buyer provides the email and the agent never receives another turn. fail if the agent receives a turn after email and does not confirm the normalized email. fail if the agent continues discovery after email. fail if the agent re-pitches after email. fail if the agent ignores buyer confirmation and keeps talking. fail if the agent never closes after email confirmation.
evaluation_repair_notes.seo_value: SEO answers should be sales-forward but non-guaranteed.
evaluation_repair_notes.elite_operating_contract: soft agreement does not immediately trigger email capture; accepted mockup without email triggers email capture; buyer gives email -> agent confirms normalized email -> buyer confirms -> agent closes; gatekeeper pass-along plus callback closes cleanly; SEO answer is confident but non-guaranteed; cost drivers explain real project complexity; salon Instagram objection gets a real difference, not generic one-place language; repeated clearer homepage as main value fails; disqualification when buyer only wants guaranteed SEO or pay-per-lead.
evaluation_repair_notes.elite_consistency_cleanup: That makes sense alone does not trigger email capture. Okay, I see what you mean is soft agreement, not a send commitment. Accepted mockup without email triggers email capture. Email provided triggers normalized email confirmation. Email confirmation triggers short close. Business-impact answers do not start with caveat unless buyer asked for guarantee. Universal value guidance does not conflict with prompt. Campaign profile does not contain major state-machine behavior blocks. SEO answer is confident but non-guaranteed. Cost answer explains real cost drivers. No guaranteed customer/ranking/revenue claims. No clearer page/homepage/path as main value argument.
evaluation_repair_notes.compact_prompt_hygiene_029: Active compact-package hygiene: no buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; repeated same-issue challenges require a different mechanism or disqualification; scripted example echo fails; clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path cannot be the headline value; soft agreement alone is not email capture; email provided triggers normalized email confirmation; email confirmation closes; stop requests stop; gatekeepers with callback windows do not get a full pitch.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Apex Plumbing in Denver. They are direct, busy, and skeptical because most urgent plumbing leads already come through Google calls. They should challenge why a plumber needs a website when people search, call the Google listing, and want fast help. They should ask whether the agent is promising more emergency jobs and should push back if the agent sounds like a generic restaurant or menu pitch. If the agent earns enough trust, the user may agree to receive the free mockup link or ask for a short callback.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent states the reason early, adapts to a plumbing business, acknowledges Google calls may already work, and gives one concrete non-guaranteed value angle such as service-area clarity, emergency/non-emergency service separation, a search-friendly page people can check before calling, license/insurance visibility only if the buyer raises trust, tap-to-call, or one page the owner controls. It should not promise more jobs, faster dispatch, higher rankings, or emergency-call lift. If the buyer asks about the catch, it should answer directly that the mockup is free to review with no obligation. If the buyer asks whether the website will get more emergency calls, the agent should start with a short boundary such as `No, I can't promise that.` or `Not as a guarantee.` and then give the emergency service-area, review, and tap-to-call mechanism; it fails if the main answer is only clearer page, potential customers something to judge, or initial judgments. If the buyer accepts the send path before giving contact details, the agent should ask for the email or other approved send path before ending. If the buyer gives an email, the agent must confirm the normalized email only; after the buyer confirms, it must close naturally. If the buyer asks when the email will arrive, the agent must answer timing directly and briefly. It should use short non-guarantee wording and must not use long wording such as `I can't promise that a website will automatically...` unless a stricter compliance boundary is needed. It fails if the agent receives a turn after email and does not confirm the normalized email, continues discovery after email, re-pitches after email, ignores buyer confirmation, never closes after email confirmation, uses restaurant leakage such as food menu, reservations, tables, food ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language unless Mike appears in buyer-provided contact details, attacks Google, repeats the same website-value point across objections, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, keeps pitching after a clear no, leaves a final buyer question unanswered, or claims results that are not in the dynamic variables. Global hygiene failure: fail if any buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; if the buyer asks for a clearer answer, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies when the buyer asks for a clearer answer; fail if Emma uses clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path as the headline value; asks for email after soft agreement only; asks for email again after email was already provided; continues selling after email confirmation; keeps pitching after stop request; or gives a full pitch to a gatekeeper after a callback window. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.
